How does AI monitoring work in a testing center?
The exam launches in the Talview Secure Browser on the test center device. AI then monitors and records video, audio and screen activity, and flags signs such as second voices, device tampering and off-screen glances. Alerts go to the in-room proctor in real time, and each session is stored with logs, recordings and flag reports.
Does in-center proctoring replace the proctors in our test center?
No. It adds a layer to them. The
exam proctor
keeps watching the physical room, while AI watches the digital environment and alerts the proctor when something needs action.
Can in-center proctoring help with proctor-candidate collusion?
It makes collusion harder to hide. Every session is recorded with logs and flag reports, and AI flags events such as proctor absence, so what happened in the session is on the record, not only in one person's account.
What evidence is available if a test-taker disputes a result?
Each session is stored with logs, recordings and flag reports. That evidence is ready for audits, compliance checks or disputes, so your team can decide on the record.
What devices and platforms does it support?
Windows desktops and laptops, and your existing test platform through an API or SDK.
Run one exam through it. Then decide.
One exam. One requisition. Thirty to sixty days. See it on your own sessions before you commit to anything larger.
